49441.q: Which valuable metal has been mined in South Africa for a long time?
49441.e: South Africa has large gold mines. Some of them are several kilometres deep.
49441.m: South Africa is known for its deep gold mines.

49442.q: Which animals can you see in the wild in South Africa?
49442.e: South Africa is at the southern tip of Africa. Lions, elephants, rhinos and giraffes live in its national parks.
49442.m: Lions and elephants live in South Africa.

49443.q: What is the capital of Nigeria?
49443.e: Abuja has been the capital of Nigeria since 1991. The city was built specially for this in the middle of the country.
49443.m: Abuja is the capital of Nigeria.

49444.q: Which city is the largest city in Nigeria?
49444.e: Lagos is on the coast and is the largest city in Nigeria. It used to be the capital too.
49444.m: Lagos is the largest city in Nigeria.

49445.q: Which large river is Nigeria named after?
49445.e: The Niger flows through Nigeria and into the Atlantic. The country bears its name.
49445.m: Nigeria is named after the River Niger.

49446.q: What is the official language of Nigeria?
49446.e: Nigeria used to be a British colony. That is why English is the official language, and there are hundreds of other languages too.
49446.m: English is the official language in Nigeria.

49447.q: What colours is the flag of Nigeria?
49447.e: Nigeria's flag has three vertical stripes: green, white, green. Green stands for the land and nature.
49447.m: The flag of Nigeria is green and white.

49448.q: What is Nigeria's large film industry called?
49448.e: A great many films are made in Nigeria every year. This film industry is called Nollywood.
49448.m: Nigeria's film industry is called Nollywood.

49449.q: Which natural resource is especially important for Nigeria?
49449.e: Nigeria has large oil reserves. Oil is the country's most important export.

49450.q: What is the capital of Ethiopia?
49450.e: Addis Ababa is the capital of Ethiopia. The name means “new flower”.
49450.m: Addis Ababa is the capital of Ethiopia.

49451.q: Which drink originally comes from Ethiopia?
49451.e: The coffee plant originally comes from the highlands of Ethiopia. Coffee is still very important there today.

49452.q: What is the famous skeleton, over three million years old, that was found in Ethiopia called?
49452.e: Lucy was found in Ethiopia in 1974. She is one of the ancestors of humans and lived about 3.2 million years ago. Ötzi is much younger, and Sue is a dinosaur.
49452.m: The skeleton Lucy from Ethiopia is over three million years old.

49453.e: Ethiopia has no coast. Like Switzerland, it is a landlocked country.
49453.m: Ethiopia is not by the sea, just like Switzerland.

49454.q: What is the large, soft flatbread from Ethiopia called?
49454.e: Injera is a thin, slightly sour flatbread. People use it to eat their food, without any cutlery.
49454.m: In Ethiopia people eat injera, a soft flatbread.

49455.q: Which river starts at Lake Tana in Ethiopia?
49455.e: The Blue Nile flows out of Lake Tana. Later, in Sudan, it meets the White Nile, which comes from further south.
49455.m: The Blue Nile begins at Lake Tana in Ethiopia.

49456.q: How many months does the calendar in Ethiopia have?
49456.e: The Ethiopian calendar has twelve months of 30 days each. On top of that there is a short thirteenth month with 5 or 6 days.

49457.q: What is special about the old churches of Lalibela in Ethiopia?
a: They are carved out of the rock
They stand on stilts in the water
49457.e: In Lalibela, eleven churches were carved out of the rock about 800 years ago. They are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
49457.m: Lalibela has churches carved out of the rock.

49458.q: Which animals can you watch in Gombe National Park in Tanzania?
49458.e: In Gombe National Park, Jane Goodall studied the chimpanzees for decades. They live there in the forest by the lake shore.
49458.m: Chimpanzees live in Gombe National Park in Tanzania.

49459.q: What is the money in Tanzania called?
49459.e: In Tanzania people pay with the Tanzanian shilling. Kenya and Uganda also have a currency called the shilling.
49459.m: In Tanzania people pay with the shilling.

49460.q: What is the well-known island off the coast of Tanzania called?
49460.e: Zanzibar belongs to Tanzania and lies in the Indian Ocean. The island is known for spices such as cloves.
49460.m: Zanzibar is a spice island belonging to Tanzania.

49461.q: Which large animals live in Tanzania's national parks?
49461.e: Tanzania is in Africa. Lots of elephants, lions, giraffes and zebras live in its national parks.
49461.m: Lots of elephants live in Tanzania.

49462.e: Tanzania is in the east of Africa. It has large national parks with lots of wild animals.

49463.q: Which city is the largest city in Tanzania?
49463.e: Dar es Salaam is on the Indian Ocean and is the largest city in Tanzania. It has the country's most important port.
49463.m: Dar es Salaam is the largest city in Tanzania.

49465.q: Which long and very deep lake lies on the western border of Tanzania?
49465.e: Lake Tanganyika is very long and one of the deepest lakes in the world. It lies between Tanzania and the Congo.
49465.m: Lake Tanganyika is one of the deepest lakes in the world.

49466.q: What is the capital of Ghana?
49466.e: Accra is the capital of Ghana. It is on the coast of the Gulf of Guinea.
49466.m: Accra is the capital of Ghana.

49467.q: Which raw material for chocolate is grown a lot in Ghana?
49467.e: Ghana is one of the largest cocoa producers in the world. Chocolate is made from cocoa beans.
49467.m: Ghana grows lots of cocoa for chocolate.

49468.q: What was Ghana called in the past, when it was a British colony?
49468.e: Ghana used to be called the Gold Coast. The name comes from the large amount of gold found there.
49468.m: Ghana used to be called the Gold Coast.

49469.q: In which year did Ghana become independent?
49469.e: Ghana became independent from Great Britain in 1957. It was one of the first countries in Africa to become free.

49470.q: What is the huge reservoir in Ghana called?
49470.e: Lake Volta was created by a dam on the River Volta. It is one of the largest artificial lakes in the world.
49470.m: Lake Volta in Ghana is a huge reservoir.

49471.q: What is the official language of Ghana?
49471.e: Because Ghana was a British colony, English is the official language. Many people also speak Twi.
49471.m: English is the official language in Ghana.

49472.q: What can you see in the middle of Ghana's flag?
49472.e: Ghana's flag has red, gold and green stripes. In the middle there is a black star.
49472.m: There is a black star on Ghana's flag.

49473.q: What is the capital of Senegal?
49473.e: Dakar is the capital of Senegal. It lies on a peninsula on the Atlantic.
49473.m: Dakar is the capital of Senegal.

49474.q: In which country is the westernmost point of mainland Africa?
49474.e: The westernmost point of mainland Africa is near Dakar in Senegal. It is called Pointe des Almadies.
49474.m: The westernmost point of mainland Africa is in Senegal.

49475.q: What is the official language of Senegal?
49475.e: Senegal used to be a French colony. That is why French is the official language, and many people also speak Wolof.
49475.m: French is the official language in Senegal.

49476.q: Which famous motor race used to end in the capital of Senegal?
49476.e: The Dakar Rally used to run from Europe right across the Sahara to Dakar. Today it takes place somewhere else.
49476.m: The Dakar Rally used to end in Senegal.

49477.q: What special colour is Lake Retba in Senegal often?
49477.e: Lake Retba is also called “Lac Rose”, the pink lake. Tiny algae in the very salty water turn it pink.
49477.m: Lake Retba in Senegal often glows pink.

49478.q: Which small country is almost completely surrounded by Senegal?
49478.e: Gambia lies like a narrow strip along a river. It is almost completely surrounded by Senegal.
49478.m: Gambia lies almost completely inside Senegal.

49479.q: Which thick tree is a symbol of Senegal?
49479.e: The baobab, also called the monkey-bread tree, has a very thick trunk. It appears on Senegal's coat of arms.
49479.m: The baobab is a symbol of Senegal.

49480.q: Which city is the capital of Egypt?
49480.e: Cairo is the capital and largest city of Egypt. Over 20 million people live in the city and the area around it.
49480.m: Cairo is the capital of Egypt.

49481.q: Which famous ancient buildings stand right next to the city of Cairo in Egypt?
49481.e: Right on the edge of Cairo is Giza with the great pyramids. They are over 4,000 years old.
49481.m: The pyramids stand next to Cairo.

49482.q: Which language do most people in Cairo speak?
49482.e: In Cairo and all over Egypt people speak Arabic. It is the country's official language.

49483.q: What nickname does Cairo have because of its many mosques?
49483.e: A minaret is the tower of a mosque. Because Cairo has so many of them, it is called the “City of a Thousand Minarets”.
49483.m: Cairo is also called the “City of a Thousand Minarets”.

49484.q: There is a large bazaar in Cairo. What is a bazaar?
a: A market with lots of stalls
49484.e: A bazaar is a large market. In Cairo people sell spices, lamps and jewellery there.
49484.m: A bazaar is a large market.

49485.q: One of the oldest universities in the world is in Cairo. About how old is it?
49485.e: Al-Azhar in Cairo is over 1,000 years old. It is one of the oldest universities in the world.
49485.m: Cairo has a university that is over 1,000 years old.

49486.q: Which means of transport runs underground in Cairo?
49486.e: Cairo has had an underground railway, the Metro, since 1987. It was the first underground railway in Africa.
49486.m: Cairo has Africa's first underground railway.

49487.q: What is the flat mountain above Cape Town called?
49487.e: Table Mountain is completely flat on top, like a table. It is the landmark of Cape Town.
49487.m: Table Mountain is the landmark of Cape Town.

49488.q: How can you travel up Table Mountain in Cape Town in comfort?
a: by a lift inside the rock
49488.e: A cable car takes visitors up Table Mountain. Its cabin turns during the ride, so you can see all around.
49488.m: A cable car with a rotating cabin goes up Table Mountain.

49489.q: Which animals can you see at Boulders Beach near Cape Town?
49489.e: A colony of African penguins lives at Boulders Beach. You can watch them from close up.
49489.m: Penguins live on the beach near Cape Town.

49490.q: On which island off Cape Town was Nelson Mandela imprisoned for many years?
49490.e: Robben Island used to be a prison island. Today it is a museum and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
49490.m: Nelson Mandela was imprisoned on Robben Island.

49491.q: Which well-known cape lies south of Cape Town?
49491.e: The Cape of Good Hope is on a peninsula south of Cape Town. Sailors sailed round it on the way to India.
49491.m: The Cape of Good Hope lies south of Cape Town.

49492.q: Which important South African institution is based in Cape Town?
49492.e: South Africa's Parliament meets in Cape Town. The government, however, works in Pretoria.
49492.m: South Africa's Parliament meets in Cape Town.

49493.q: What is the Bo-Kaap district in Cape Town known for?
49493.e: In the Bo-Kaap the houses are painted in bright colours. The district is a popular spot for photos.
49493.m: The Bo-Kaap in Cape Town has colourful houses.

49494.q: Which ocean is Cape Town on?
49494.e: Cape Town is on Table Bay on the Atlantic Ocean. The water there is often quite cool.
49494.m: Cape Town is on the Atlantic.

49495.q: Which city is the capital of Kenya?
49495.e: Nairobi is the capital and largest city of Kenya. It lies in the highlands in the south of the country.
49495.m: Nairobi is the capital of Kenya.

49496.q: What is special about the national park on the edge of Nairobi?
a: Wild animals in front of tower blocks
49496.e: Nairobi National Park is right next to the city. You can see giraffes and rhinos with tower blocks in the background.
49496.m: In Nairobi National Park you see wild animals in front of the city.

49497.q: What does the name Nairobi mean?
49497.e: The name comes from the Maa language. “Enkare Nairobi” means roughly “cool water”.

49498.q: At about what altitude is Nairobi?
49498.e: Nairobi lies in the highlands, at about 1,600 to 1,800 metres above sea level depending on the district. That is why it is quite mild there even though it is near the equator.
49498.m: Nairobi lies high up at about 1,700 metres.

49499.q: Which UN environmental organisation has its headquarters in Nairobi?
49499.e: UNEP is the United Nations Environment Programme. Its headquarters are in Nairobi.
49499.m: The UN Environment Programme is based in Nairobi.

49500.q: How did Nairobi begin towards the end of the 19th century?
a: as a camp for railway building
as a harbour by the sea
49500.e: Nairobi began in 1896 as a camp during the building of the Uganda Railway. The small camp soon became a big city.
49500.m: Nairobi began as a camp during the building of a railway.

49501.q: Which animals are raised in a well-known orphanage in Nairobi?
49501.e: In Nairobi National Park there is an orphanage for baby elephants. Later they are taken back to the wild.
49501.m: Orphaned elephants are raised in Nairobi.

49502.q: What is the largest of the pyramids of Giza called?
49502.e: The Pyramid of Khufu, also called the Great Pyramid, is the largest pyramid at Giza. It was built for the pharaoh Khufu.
49502.m: The Pyramid of Khufu is the largest pyramid at Giza.

49503.q: How many large pyramids stand at Giza?
49503.e: There are three large pyramids at Giza. They belong to the pharaohs Khufu, Khafre and Menkaure.
49503.m: There are three large pyramids at Giza.

49504.q: What were the pyramids of Giza built for?
49504.e: The pyramids were huge tombs. The pharaohs were meant to rest in them after their death.
49504.m: The pyramids were tombs for pharaohs.

49505.q: Which mythical creature with a lion's body and a human head lies in front of the pyramids?
49505.e: The Great Sphinx of Giza has the body of a lion and the head of a human. It is carved out of the rock.
49505.m: The Sphinx has a lion's body and a human head.

49506.q: What were the pyramids of Giza built from?
49506.e: The pyramids are made of millions of stone blocks, mainly limestone. Some blocks weigh several tonnes.
49506.m: The pyramids are built from huge stone blocks.

49507.q: About how tall was the Pyramid of Khufu originally?
49507.e: The Pyramid of Khufu was originally about 146 metres tall. Today it is a little lower because its tip is missing.
49507.m: The Pyramid of Khufu used to be about 146 metres tall.

49508.q: About how old are the pyramids of Giza?
49508.e: The pyramids were built more than 4,500 years ago. They are among the oldest buildings in the world.
49508.m: The pyramids of Giza are over 4,500 years old.

49509.q: Which material for writing on was invented in China?
49509.e: Paper was invented in China about 2,000 years ago. Later it reached Europe by way of Arabia.

49510.q: What is the main colour of China's flag?
49510.e: China's flag is red. At the top left there are yellow stars.
49510.m: China's flag is red with yellow stars.

49511.q: How many yellow stars are there on China's flag?
49511.e: On China's red flag there is one large and four small yellow stars. That makes 5 stars altogether.
49511.m: China's flag has five yellow stars.

49512.q: What is the longest river in China called?
49512.e: The Yangtze is the longest river in China and in the whole of Asia. It is over 6,000 kilometres long. The Yellow River is China's second-longest river.
49512.m: The Yangtze is the longest river in China.

49513.q: What do many people in China eat their food with?
49513.e: In China people often eat with two thin chopsticks. They are made of wood, bamboo or plastic.
49513.m: In China people often eat with chopsticks.

49514.q: Which big festival is celebrated in China in January or February?
49514.e: Chinese New Year is also called the Spring Festival. There are fireworks, red lanterns and dragon dances.
49514.m: In China the New Year festival is celebrated in January or February.

49515.q: Which language do most people in China speak?
49515.e: Most people in China speak Chinese. It is written with many characters instead of letters.
49515.m: In China people mainly speak Chinese.

49516.q: Which wrestling sport for heavy men is a national sport of Japan?
49516.e: In sumo, two heavy wrestlers try to push their opponent out of a circle. Sumo is very old and popular in Japan.
49516.m: Sumo is a form of wrestling from Japan.

49517.q: What does the flag of Japan look like?
49517.e: Japan's flag is white. In the middle there is a red circle that stands for the sun.
49517.m: Japan's flag is white with a red circle.

49518.q: What other name does Japan have?
49518.e: Seen from China, the sun rises in the east over Japan. That is why Japan is called the “Land of the Rising Sun”.
49518.m: Japan is also called the Land of the Rising Sun.

49519.q: Which Japanese food is made of rice and often raw fish?
49519.e: Sushi is a well-known dish from Japan. It is made of rice and often topped with raw fish.
49519.m: Sushi is a Japanese food made of rice and fish.

49520.q: What is the very fast train in Japan called?
49520.e: The Shinkansen is Japan's high-speed train. It has been running since 1964 and is very punctual.
49520.m: The Shinkansen is Japan's high-speed train.

49521.q: What is the Japanese art of folding paper called?
49521.e: In origami you fold a sheet of paper into shapes, for example a crane. You do not need scissors.
49521.m: Origami is the Japanese art of paper folding.

49522.q: What is the money in Japan called?
49522.e: In Japan people pay with the yen. Its symbol is ¥.
49522.m: In Japan people pay with yen.

49523.q: Which blossoms do people in Japan celebrate every spring?
49523.e: In spring the cherry trees in Japan blossom pink and white. Many families then have a picnic under the trees.
49523.m: In Japan people celebrate the cherry blossom in spring.

49524.e: “To” means east and “kyo” means capital. The name was chosen in 1868.

49525.q: About how many people live in the Greater Tokyo area?
49525.e: Well over 30 million people live in the Greater Tokyo area. That is more than three times as many as in the whole of Switzerland.
49525.m: Greater Tokyo is one of the largest urban areas in the world.

49526.q: Which city hosted the Summer Olympic Games that took place in 2021?
49526.e: The Games were called “Tokyo 2020”. Because of the coronavirus pandemic they only took place in summer 2021.
49526.m: The 2020 Summer Olympics took place in Tokyo in 2021.

49527.q: What was Tokyo called in the past?
49527.e: The city used to be called Edo. At that time it was the city of the powerful shoguns.
49527.m: Tokyo used to be called Edo.

49528.q: What is the tallest tower in Tokyo called?
49528.e: The Tokyo Skytree is 634 metres tall. It is the tallest tower in Japan. The older Tokyo Tower is much smaller.
49528.m: The Tokyo Skytree is the tallest tower in Japan.

49529.e: Tokyo is on Tokyo Bay. This bay is part of the Pacific Ocean.

49530.q: What is the Shibuya Crossing in Tokyo known for?
49530.e: At the Shibuya Crossing all the traffic lights turn green at the same time. Then thousands of people walk across the road in all directions.
49530.m: Huge numbers of pedestrians cross the Shibuya Crossing in Tokyo.

49531.q: What is the money in India called?
49531.e: In India people pay with the Indian rupee. Mahatma Gandhi is shown on the banknotes.
49531.m: In India people pay with rupees.

49532.q: Which river is sacred to many people in India?
49532.e: The Ganges is a sacred river for Hindus. Many people bathe in it to pray.
49532.m: The Ganges is a sacred river in India.

49533.q: What is the big film industry in the Indian city of Mumbai called?
49533.e: The name Bollywood is made from Bombay, the old name of Mumbai, and Hollywood. The films often have lots of music and dancing.
49533.m: Bollywood is the film industry in Mumbai.

49534.q: Which animal is considered sacred in Hinduism in India?
49534.e: In Hinduism the cow is sacred. That is why cows wander freely along the streets in India.
49534.m: In Hinduism the cow is considered sacred.

49535.q: Which sport is the most popular in India?
49535.e: Cricket is a game with a bat and ball. In India millions of people watch the matches.
49535.m: Cricket is the most popular sport in India.

49536.q: What is the heavy rainy season in India in summer called?
49536.e: The monsoon is a wind that brings lots of rain from the sea to India in summer. The farmers need the rain for their fields.
49536.m: The monsoon brings lots of rain to India in summer.

49537.q: Which large animal is the national animal of Thailand?
49537.e: The Asian elephant is Thailand's national animal. In the past elephants worked in the forest and carried heavy tree trunks.
49537.m: The elephant is Thailand's national animal.

49538.q: What is the money in Thailand called?
49538.e: In Thailand people pay with the baht. The king is shown on the banknotes.
49538.m: In Thailand people pay with baht.

49539.q: How do you greet someone politely in Thailand?
a: Put your hands together and bow
49539.e: The greeting in Thailand is called the wai. You put your palms together in front of your chest and bow your head.
49539.m: In Thailand people greet each other with their hands together and a bow.

49540.q: What is a tuk-tuk in Thailand?
49540.e: A tuk-tuk is a small, open taxi with three wheels. Its name comes from the sound of its engine.
49540.m: A tuk-tuk is a three-wheeled taxi.

49541.q: What religion do most people in Thailand follow?
49541.e: Most people in Thailand are Buddhists. The country has thousands of temples with golden Buddha figures.
49541.m: Most people in Thailand are Buddhists.

49542.q: About how many islands make up Indonesia?
49542.e: Indonesia is the largest island country in the world. It has over 17,000 islands, but nobody lives on many of them.
49542.m: Indonesia is made up of over 17,000 islands.

49543.q: Which city on the island of Java is the largest city in Indonesia?
49543.e: Jakarta is on the island of Java and has long been the capital. On the island of Borneo, Indonesia is building a new capital called Nusantara (as of 2025).
49543.m: Jakarta is the largest city in Indonesia.

49544.q: Which is the largest lizard in the world and lives in Indonesia?
49544.e: The Komodo dragon can grow to about 3 metres long. It only lives on a few islands in Indonesia.
49544.m: The Komodo dragon is the largest lizard in the world.

49545.q: Which ape with red fur lives in the rainforests of Asia?
49545.e: Orangutans live in the rainforests on large islands in Asia. Their name means “person of the forest”.
49545.m: The orangutan is an ape with red fur.

49546.q: Which country does the popular holiday island of Bali belong to?
49546.e: Bali is an Indonesian island with beaches, rice fields and many temples. Millions of holidaymakers come every year.
49546.m: Bali is a popular holiday island in Indonesia.

49547.q: Which volcano in Indonesia erupted violently in 1883?
49547.e: Krakatoa lies between the islands of Java and Sumatra. The bang from its eruption in 1883 could be heard very far away.

49548.q: Which imaginary line around the Earth runs right through Indonesia?
49548.e: The equator divides the Earth into a northern half and a southern half. It runs right through Indonesia, which is why it is always warm there.
49548.m: The equator runs right through Indonesia.

49549.q: What was Ho Chi Minh City in Vietnam called in the past?
49549.e: Vietnam's largest city used to be called Saigon. Since 1976 it has been called Ho Chi Minh City.
49549.m: Ho Chi Minh City used to be called Saigon.

49550.q: What shape is Vietnam on the map?
a: Long and narrow like an S
49550.e: Vietnam is very long from north to south, but in some places only about 50 kilometres wide. It looks like an S.
49550.m: Vietnam is long and narrow like an S.

49551.q: What is Ha Long Bay in Vietnam famous for?
a: Lots of rocks in the sea
49551.e: In Ha Long Bay almost 2,000 limestone rocks rise out of the sea. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
49551.m: In Ha Long Bay lots of rocks rise out of the sea.

49552.q: Which plant do farmers in Vietnam often grow in wet fields?
49552.e: Rice grows well in fields that are under water. Vietnam sells a great deal of rice to other countries.
49552.m: Lots of rice is grown in Vietnam.

49553.q: Which noodle soup is a typical dish from Vietnam?
49553.e: Pho is a soup with rice noodles, herbs and meat. In Vietnam people often eat it for breakfast.
49553.m: Pho is a noodle soup from Vietnam.

49554.q: Which large river flows into the sea in the south of Vietnam?
49554.e: The Mekong flows through several countries. In the south of Vietnam it splits into many branches and flows into the sea.
49554.m: The Mekong flows into the sea in Vietnam.

49555.q: What is the capital of South Korea?
49555.e: Seoul is the capital and largest city of South Korea. About half of all the people in the country live in the greater Seoul area.
49555.m: Seoul is the capital of South Korea.

49556.q: Which country borders South Korea to the north?
49556.e: Korea has been divided into two states since 1948. North Korea is in the north, South Korea in the south.
49556.m: North Korea lies north of South Korea.

49557.q: What is the spicy pickled cabbage dish from Korea called?
49557.e: Kimchi is cabbage pickled with chilli and garlic. In Korea people eat it with almost every meal.
49557.m: Kimchi is a spicy cabbage dish from Korea.

49558.q: Where did the 2018 Winter Olympics take place?
49558.e: The 2018 Winter Olympics were in Pyeongchang. That is a mountain region in South Korea.
49558.m: The 2018 Winter Olympics took place in South Korea.

49559.q: What is the Korean alphabet called?
49559.e: The Hangul alphabet was invented about 600 years ago. It has only a few letters and is easy to learn.
49559.m: The Korean alphabet is called Hangul.

49560.q: Which martial art comes from Korea?
49560.e: Taekwondo comes from Korea. Fighters mainly use fast kicks.
49560.m: Taekwondo is a martial art from Korea.

49561.q: What is the money in South Korea called?
49561.e: In South Korea people pay with the won. One Swiss franc is worth more than 1,000 won.
49561.m: In South Korea people pay with won.

49562.q: What is the capital of Mongolia?
49562.e: Ulaanbaatar is also spelled Ulan Bator. Almost half the people of Mongolia live there.
49562.m: Ulaanbaatar is the capital of Mongolia.

49563.q: What are people in Mongolia called who move from place to place with their herds?
49563.e: Nomads do not have a fixed house in one place. They move with their animals to wherever there is fresh grass.
49563.m: Nomads move from place to place with their herds.

49564.q: Which large desert lies in the south of Mongolia?
49564.e: The Gobi Desert is in Mongolia and China. It is hot there in summer and freezing cold in winter.
49564.m: The Gobi Desert is in Mongolia.

49565.q: What was the name of the famous ruler of the Mongols who founded a huge empire?
49565.e: About 800 years ago Genghis Khan united the Mongol peoples. He founded the Mongol Empire.
49565.m: Genghis Khan founded the Mongol Empire.

49566.q: Which rare wild horse lives free in Mongolia again today?
49566.e: Przewalski's horse had almost died out in the wild. Zoos bred the animals and released them back into the wild in Mongolia.
49566.m: Przewalski's horse lives free in Mongolia again.

49567.q: Which animals are there far more of than people in Mongolia?
49567.e: In Mongolia many families keep large herds. There are many millions of sheep, but only about 3.5 million people.
49567.m: In Mongolia there are more sheep than people.

49568.q: Which contests take place at the Naadam festival in Mongolia?
49568.e: Naadam is the biggest festival in Mongolia. People compete in wrestling, horse racing and archery.
49568.m: At the Naadam festival there is riding, wrestling and archery.

49569.q: Which word do people use to greet each other in Nepal?
49569.e: In Nepal people say “Namaste”. While saying it, they put their hands together in front of their chest.
49569.m: In Nepal people greet each other with Namaste.

49570.q: What is the capital of Nepal?
49570.e: Kathmandu lies in a valley in the middle of Nepal. The city has many old temples.
49570.m: Kathmandu is the capital of Nepal.

49571.q: What is special about the flag of Nepal?
49571.e: Nepal's flag is made of two triangles one above the other. It is the only national flag that is not rectangular.

49572.q: What is the mountain people of Nepal called whose members often accompany climbers?
49572.e: The Sherpa live high in the mountains of Nepal. Many work as porters and mountain guides.
49572.m: The Sherpa often accompany climbers in Nepal.

49573.q: In which mountain range is the north of Nepal?
49573.e: The Himalayas are the highest mountains on Earth. Many of their highest peaks are in Nepal.

49574.q: In which place in Nepal was the Buddha born?
49574.e: According to tradition, the Buddha was born in Lumbini in the south of Nepal. Today the place is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
49574.m: The Buddha was born in Lumbini in Nepal.

49575.q: Which long-haired kind of cattle lives high in the mountains of Nepal?
49575.e: The yak has thick, long fur against the cold. It carries loads and gives milk and wool.
49575.m: The yak is a long-haired kind of cattle.

49576.q: What is the capital of the Philippines?
49576.e: Manila is on the island of Luzon and is the capital of the Philippines. The city is very densely populated.
49576.m: Manila is the capital of the Philippines.

49577.q: About how many islands make up the Philippines?
49577.e: The Philippines are made up of over 7,000 islands. The largest are called Luzon and Mindanao.
49577.m: The Philippines are made up of over 7,000 islands.

49578.q: Who are the Philippines named after?
49578.e: The islands were named after Philip II, who later became King of Spain. Spain ruled the Philippines for over 300 years.
49578.m: The Philippines are named after the Spanish king Philip II.

49579.q: Which small animal with huge eyes lives in the Philippines?
49579.e: The Philippine tarsier is only as big as a hand. Its eyes are huge compared with its body.

49580.q: What are the colourful shared taxis in the Philippines called?
49580.e: Jeepneys were built from old army jeeps and painted in bright colours. They are a popular way to get around.
49580.m: Jeepneys are colourful shared taxis in the Philippines.

49581.q: What are the round hills on the island of Bohol that turn brown in the dry season called?
49581.e: There are over 1,000 round hills on Bohol. In the dry season the grass turns brown, and then they look like chocolate.
49581.m: The Chocolate Hills on Bohol look like chocolate.

49582.q: Which strong storms often hit the Philippines?
49582.e: A typhoon is a strong tropical storm over the Pacific. Several typhoons pass over the Philippines every year.
49582.m: The Philippines are often hit by typhoons.

49583.q: Which country is Beijing the capital of?
49583.e: Beijing is the capital of the People's Republic of China. In English it used to be called Peking.
49583.m: Beijing is the capital of China.

49584.q: What is the huge old imperial palace in Beijing called?
49584.e: The Chinese emperors used to live in the Forbidden City. Ordinary people were not allowed in, hence the name.
49584.m: The Forbidden City was the emperors' palace in Beijing.

49585.q: In which year did Beijing host the Summer Olympic Games?
49585.e: The 2008 Summer Olympics were in Beijing. The opening ceremony began on 8.8.2008.
49585.m: Beijing hosted the Summer Olympics in 2008.

49586.q: What is special about Beijing and the Olympic Games?
a: Both Summer and Winter Games took place there
The very first Olympic Games took place there
The Summer Games took place there three times
Only Winter Games took place there
49586.e: Beijing hosted the Summer Games in 2008 and the Winter Games in 2022 as well. No other city had managed that before.
49586.m: Both Summer and Winter Games took place in Beijing.

49587.q: What do you eat the famous Peking duck from China with?
49587.e: For Peking duck, the duck is roasted until crispy. It is eaten with thin pancakes and sauce.
49587.m: Peking duck is eaten with thin pancakes.

49588.q: What is the round temple in Beijing where the emperors prayed for a good harvest called?
49588.e: The emperors used to pray for a good harvest at the Temple of Heaven. The round hall has a blue roof.
49588.m: At the Temple of Heaven the emperors prayed for a good harvest.

49589.q: What does the Chinese name “Beijing” mean?
49589.e: “Bei” means north and “jing” means capital. The city is in the north of the country.

49590.q: Why was the Great Wall of China built?
49590.e: The wall was meant to protect the country from horse-riding peoples from the north. Soldiers guarded it.
49590.m: The Great Wall of China was meant to protect against attackers.

49591.q: How long is the Great Wall of China with all its parts together?
49591.e: A survey in 2012 found that all the sections together come to over 21,000 kilometres. It is the longest structure in the world.
49591.m: The Great Wall of China is over 20,000 kilometres long.

49592.q: Can you see the Great Wall of China from the moon with the naked eye?
49592.e: The wall is very long, but only a few metres wide. That is why you cannot see it from the moon.
49592.m: You cannot see the Great Wall of China from the moon.

49593.q: What stands at intervals along the Great Wall of China?
49593.e: There are many watchtowers on the wall. From them, soldiers could spot enemies early and send signals with smoke.
49593.m: There are many watchtowers on the Great Wall of China.

49594.q: How long did people spend building the Great Wall of China?
49594.e: Different emperors had the wall built over many centuries. The best-known parts are about 500 years old.
49594.m: The Great Wall of China was built over many hundreds of years.

49595.q: What are the best-known parts of the Great Wall of China built from?
49595.e: The best-known parts are made of stones and fired bricks. Older parts are made of rammed earth.
49595.m: The Great Wall of China is built of stone, bricks and earth.

49596.q: What do many tourists do on the Great Wall of China today?
49596.e: Every year millions of people walk along the wall. Some sections are very steep with lots of steps.
49596.m: You can walk along the Great Wall of China.

49597.q: In which country is the Taj Mahal?
49597.e: The Taj Mahal is in the north of India. It is one of the best-known buildings in the world.
49597.m: The Taj Mahal is in India.

49598.q: Why did a ruler have the Taj Mahal built?
a: As a tomb for his wife
As a palace to live in
As a temple for the gods
49598.e: The Mughal emperor Shah Jahan had the Taj Mahal built for his late wife Mumtaz Mahal. It is a sign of his love.
49598.m: The Taj Mahal is a tomb for a beloved wife.

49599.q: Which white stone is the Taj Mahal built from?
49599.e: The Taj Mahal is made of white marble. Depending on the light, it shimmers pink, white or golden.
49599.m: The Taj Mahal is made of white marble.

49600.q: Where does the Taj Mahal stand?
a: In the middle of the desert
49600.e: The Taj Mahal stands on the bank of a river in India. The river is called the Yamuna.
49600.m: The Taj Mahal stands by a river.

49601.q: Which famous list has the Taj Mahal been on since 2007?
a: New Seven Wonders of the World
Largest railway stations in the world
49601.e: In 2007 the “New Seven Wonders of the World” were chosen. The Taj Mahal is one of them.
49601.m: The Taj Mahal is one of the New Seven Wonders of the World.

49602.q: How many slender towers stand around the Taj Mahal?
49602.e: Four slender towers, the minarets, stand around the tomb. In the middle there is a large dome.
49602.m: Four towers stand around the Taj Mahal.

49603.q: What is the famous old fortress in the centre of the Russian capital called?
49603.e: The Kremlin is a fortress with high walls, towers and churches. The Russian president works there.
49603.m: The Kremlin is the famous fortress at the heart of Moscow.

49604.q: What is the money in Russia called?
49604.e: In Russia people pay with roubles. One rouble has 100 kopecks.
49604.m: In Russia people pay with roubles.

49605.q: What are the painted wooden dolls from Russia that fit inside each other called?
49605.e: A matryoshka is hollow inside. Inside it there is a smaller doll, inside that an even smaller one, and so on.
49605.m: The matryoshka is a Russian doll with many dolls inside.

49606.q: What is the huge, cold region in the Asian part of Russia called?
49606.e: Siberia stretches from the Urals to the Pacific. The winters there are very long and freezing cold.
49606.m: Siberia is a huge, cold region in Russia.

49607.q: What is the deepest lake in the world, which lies in Siberia, called?
49607.e: Lake Baikal is over 1,600 metres deep. It is also one of the oldest lakes on Earth.
49607.m: Lake Baikal is the deepest lake in the world.

49608.q: What is the huge coniferous forest in Siberia called?
49608.e: The taiga is a forest of conifers such as spruces, pines and larches. It is the largest forest on Earth.
49608.m: The taiga is a huge coniferous forest in the north.

49609.q: What is the long railway line right across Siberia called?
49609.e: The Trans-Siberian Railway is over 9,000 kilometres long. It is the longest railway line in the world.
49609.m: The Trans-Siberian Railway runs right across Siberia.

49610.q: Which sea do Siberia's great rivers flow into?
49610.e: Great rivers such as the Ob, Yenisei and Lena flow north. They flow into the icy Arctic Ocean.
49610.m: Siberia's great rivers flow north into the Arctic Ocean.

49611.q: Which extinct animal is sometimes found well preserved in the ground in Siberia?
49611.e: Mammoths were large, hairy elephants of the Ice Age. Because the ground in Siberia is frozen, some mammoths have been preserved there as if in a fridge.
49611.m: Frozen mammoths are found in Siberia.

49612.q: What is the capital of Saudi Arabia?
49612.e: Riyadh lies in the middle of the desert. It is the capital and the largest city of the country.
49612.m: The capital of Saudi Arabia is Riyadh.

49613.q: On which peninsula is Saudi Arabia?
49613.e: Saudi Arabia covers most of the Arabian Peninsula. It lies between Africa and the rest of Asia.
49613.m: Saudi Arabia is on the Arabian Peninsula.

49614.q: Which city in Saudi Arabia is the holiest city of Islam?
49614.e: The Kaaba is in Mecca. Every year millions of Muslims go on pilgrimage there.
49614.m: Mecca is the holiest city of Islam.

49615.q: Which raw material made Saudi Arabia rich?
49615.e: Huge amounts of oil lie under the desert ground. Saudi Arabia sells it all over the world.
49615.m: Saudi Arabia became rich through oil.

49616.q: How many rivers that carry water all year round does Saudi Arabia have?
49616.e: Saudi Arabia is very dry and does not have a single river that always carries water. Drinking water comes from wells or from seawater with the salt removed.
49616.m: Saudi Arabia has no river that always carries water.

49617.q: What kind of landscape covers most of Saudi Arabia?
49617.e: Saudi Arabia is very hot and dry. Stony and sandy deserts cover most of the country.

49618.q: Which two seas does Saudi Arabia border?
49618.e: The Red Sea is to the west, the Persian Gulf to the east. In between there is a lot of desert.
49618.m: Saudi Arabia lies between the Red Sea and the Persian Gulf.

49619.q: Which language is spoken in Saudi Arabia?
49619.e: Arabic is the official language of Saudi Arabia. It is written from right to left.
49619.m: In Saudi Arabia people speak Arabic.

49620.q: What is the capital of the United Arab Emirates?
49620.e: Abu Dhabi is the country's capital. But it is not the largest city.
49620.m: The capital of the United Arab Emirates is Abu Dhabi.

49621.q: How many emirates make up the United Arab Emirates?
49621.e: The United Arab Emirates are a federation of seven emirates. Each emirate has its own ruler.
49621.m: The United Arab Emirates are made up of seven emirates.

49622.q: What is the Palm Jumeirah in the United Arab Emirates?
49622.e: The Palm Jumeirah was built up out of sand in the sea. From above it looks like a palm tree.
49622.m: The Palm Jumeirah is an artificial island shaped like a palm tree.

49623.q: What is the money in the United Arab Emirates called?
49623.e: In the United Arab Emirates people pay with dirhams. One dirham has 100 fils.
49623.m: In the United Arab Emirates people pay with dirhams.

49624.q: Which bird is an important national symbol of the United Arab Emirates?
49624.e: Hunting with falcons has a long tradition in the Emirates. The falcon is even on the country's coat of arms.
49624.m: The falcon is a symbol of the United Arab Emirates.

49625.q: Which sea are the United Arab Emirates mainly on?
49625.e: Most of the big cities of the Emirates are on the coast of the Persian Gulf. The water there is very warm.
49625.m: The United Arab Emirates are on the Persian Gulf.

49626.q: On which continent are the United Arab Emirates?
49626.e: The Emirates are on the Arabian Peninsula. It belongs to the continent of Asia.
49626.m: The United Arab Emirates are in Asia.

49627.q: In which year were the United Arab Emirates founded?
49627.e: In 1971 the emirates joined together to form one state. Before that they were under British protection.
49627.m: The United Arab Emirates have existed since 1971.

49628.q: In which city is the Burj Khalifa?
49628.e: The Burj Khalifa is in Dubai in the United Arab Emirates. Dubai is the largest city in the country.
49628.m: The Burj Khalifa is in Dubai.

49629.q: In which year was the Burj Khalifa opened?
49629.e: Building it took about six years. The tower was opened in 2010.
49629.m: The Burj Khalifa was opened in 2010.

49630.q: What is special about the Burj Khalifa in Dubai?
a: It is the tallest building in the world
It is the longest bridge in the world
It is the oldest building in the world
It is the largest railway station in the world
49630.e: The Burj Khalifa is 828 metres tall. That is about four times as tall as the tallest building in Switzerland.
49630.m: The Burj Khalifa is the tallest building in the world.

49631.q: About how many floors does the Burj Khalifa have?
49631.e: The Burj Khalifa has over 160 floors. That makes it much taller than any other building.
49631.m: The Burj Khalifa has more than 160 floors.

49632.q: Who is the Burj Khalifa named after?
49632.e: The tower is named after Khalifa bin Zayed. He was President of the United Arab Emirates and ruler of Abu Dhabi.
49632.m: The Burj Khalifa bears the name of a ruler.

49633.q: Which sea is Israel on to the west?
49633.e: To the west Israel has a long coast on the Mediterranean. Big cities such as Tel Aviv and Haifa are there.

49634.q: What is the very salty lake between Israel and Jordan called, where you float on top almost by yourself?
49634.e: The water in the Dead Sea is about ten times saltier than normal seawater. That is why you float in it like a cork.
49634.m: You cannot sink in the Dead Sea.

49635.q: Which language is mainly spoken in Israel?
49635.e: Hebrew is the main language in Israel. Like Arabic, it is written from right to left.
49635.m: In Israel people mainly speak Hebrew.

49636.q: Which city is holy to Jews, Christians and Muslims?
49636.e: Jerusalem has important holy places of three religions. They include the Western Wall, the Church of the Holy Sepulchre and the Dome of the Rock.
49636.m: Jerusalem is a holy city for three religions.

49637.q: What is the money in Israel called?
49637.e: In Israel people pay with the new shekel. One shekel has 100 agorot.
49637.m: In Israel people pay with shekels.

49638.q: Which symbol can be seen on the flag of Israel?
49638.e: Israel's flag is white with two blue stripes. In the middle is a blue Star of David.
49638.m: There is a Star of David on Israel's flag.

49639.q: What is the desert in the south of Israel called?
49639.e: The Negev covers more than half of Israel. It is dry and stony.
49639.m: The Negev Desert is in the south of Israel.

49640.q: What is the freshwater lake in the north of Israel called?
49640.e: The Sea of Galilee is fed by the River Jordan. It is also often mentioned in the Bible.
49640.m: The Sea of Galilee is in the north of Israel.

49641.q: What is the capital of Jordan?
49641.e: Amman is the capital and largest city of Jordan. The city is built on many hills.
49641.m: The capital of Jordan is Amman.

49642.q: What is the desert with red rocks in the south of Jordan called?
49642.e: Wadi Rum is a desert valley with red sand and high rocks. Many films have been made there.
49642.m: Wadi Rum is a red rocky desert in Jordan.

49643.q: Which sea is Jordan's only port on?
49643.e: Jordan has only a short stretch of coast. The port city of Aqaba is there, on the Red Sea.
49643.m: Jordan has its port on the Red Sea.

49644.q: Which part of the world does Jordan belong to?
49644.e: Jordan is in western Asia, between Israel, Syria, Iraq and Saudi Arabia. This region is called the Middle East.
49644.m: Jordan is in the Middle East.

49645.e: The houses and tombs of Petra were carved directly into the rock walls. The city is over 2,000 years old.
49645.m: Petra is a city that was carved into the rock.

49646.q: What colour is the rock in Petra?
49646.e: Petra is carved out of sandstone that glows red and pink. That is why Petra is also called the rose-red city.
49646.m: The rock of Petra glows red and pink.

49647.q: Which Swiss man made Petra known in Europe in 1812?
49647.e: Johann Ludwig Burckhardt came from a Basel family. He travelled through the Middle East in Arab clothing and reached Petra in 1812.
49647.m: A Swiss man from a Basel family made Petra known in Europe.

49648.q: What is the most famous building in Petra called?
49648.e: The Treasury has a magnificent front with columns carved into the rock. It is about 2,000 years old.
49648.m: The Treasury is the most famous building in Petra.

49649.q: What is the capital of Iran?
49649.e: Tehran is the capital and the largest city of Iran. To the north of the city there are high mountains.
49649.m: The capital of Iran is Tehran.

49650.q: What was Iran usually called in Europe in the past?
49650.e: Until 1935 the country was mostly called Persia in Europe. Today its official name is Iran.
49650.m: Iran used to be called Persia.

49651.q: Which language is mainly spoken in Iran?
49651.e: The official language of Iran is Persian. It is also called Farsi.
49651.m: In Iran people mainly speak Persian.

49652.q: What has Iran been famous for for a long time?
49652.e: Persian carpets have been knotted by hand for centuries. They are known all over the world.
49652.m: Iran is famous for its carpets.

49653.q: Which expensive spice comes mainly from Iran?
49653.e: Saffron comes from the flowers of a kind of crocus. Most of the world's saffron comes from Iran.
49653.m: Most of the world's saffron comes from Iran.

49654.q: Which nuts are grown in especially large amounts in Iran?
49654.e: Iran is one of the biggest growers of pistachios. People like to eat the green kernels roasted.
49654.m: Lots of pistachios grow in Iran.

49655.q: What is the ancient ruined city of the Persian kings in Iran called?
49655.e: About 2,500 years ago Persepolis was a magnificent capital of the Persian kings. Today you can still see columns and staircases with carvings there.
49655.m: Persepolis was the city of the ancient Persian kings.

49656.q: What is the capital of Kazakhstan?
49656.e: Astana has been the capital of Kazakhstan since 1997. But the largest city in the country is Almaty.
49656.m: The capital of Kazakhstan is Astana.

49657.q: Kazakhstan is the largest country in the world without a ...?
49657.e: Kazakhstan has no access to the open sea. No other country without a coastline is as big.
49657.m: Kazakhstan is the largest country without a coastline.

49658.q: In 1961 the first person flew into space from Kazakhstan. What was his name?
49658.e: Yuri Gagarin took off on 12 April 1961 from the Baikonur Cosmodrome. Baikonur is in Kazakhstan.
49658.m: Yuri Gagarin was the first person in space.

49659.q: What is the wide, flat grassland in Kazakhstan called?
49659.e: A large part of Kazakhstan is steppe. Mainly grasses grow there, and hardly any trees.

49660.q: Which fruit originally comes from the area around Kazakhstan?
49660.e: Wild apple trees grow in the mountains of Kazakhstan. Our apples are descended from them.
49660.m: The apple originally comes from Kazakhstan.

49661.q: Which bird do some Kazakhs hunt with, following an old tradition?
49661.e: Kazakhstan has an old tradition of hunting with golden eagles. The eagles catch foxes, for example.
49661.m: In Kazakhstan people traditionally hunt with golden eagles.

49662.q: Which country borders Kazakhstan to the north?
49662.e: Kazakhstan and Russia share a very long border. Until 1991 both were part of the Soviet Union.
49662.m: To the north, Kazakhstan borders Russia.

49663.q: Which large state was Kazakhstan part of until 1991?
49663.e: Kazakhstan was part of the Soviet Union. When it broke up in 1991, Kazakhstan became a country of its own.
49663.m: Kazakhstan has been a country of its own since 1991.

49664.q: What is the capital of Uzbekistan?
49664.e: Tashkent is the capital and the largest city of Uzbekistan. It is one of the largest cities in this region.
49664.m: The capital of Uzbekistan is Tashkent.

49665.q: Which famous old trading city with blue domes is in Uzbekistan?
49665.e: Samarkand is over 2,500 years old. The mosques and schools on Registan Square have magnificent blue domes.
49665.m: Samarkand is a famous old city in Uzbekistan.

49666.e: Uzbekistan is in the middle of Asia and has no coastline. Its neighbouring countries have no access to the open sea either.

49667.q: Which lake on the border of Uzbekistan has shrunk a great deal?
49667.e: A lot of water was taken from the rivers flowing into the Aral Sea for the fields. That is why most of the lake has dried up.
49667.m: The Aral Sea has shrunk a great deal.

49668.q: Which plant is grown in especially large amounts in Uzbekistan?
49668.e: Uzbekistan is one of the world's big cotton-growing countries. The fibres are used to make fabric for clothes.
49668.m: Lots of cotton is grown in Uzbekistan.

49669.q: What is plov, the national dish of Uzbekistan?
49669.e: Plov is rice with meat, carrots and onions. It is often cooked in a big pot.
49669.m: Plov is a rice dish from Uzbekistan.

49670.q: Which large state was Uzbekistan part of until 1991?
49670.e: Uzbekistan was part of the Soviet Union until 1991. After that it became a country of its own.

49671.q: Which part of the world does Uzbekistan belong to?
49671.e: Uzbekistan is in the middle of Asia, far from the oceans. That is why it counts as part of Central Asia.

49672.q: Which country did the silk on the Silk Road come from?
49672.e: The Chinese were the first to know how to make silk. For a long time they kept it a secret.

49673.q: Which famous traveller from Venice went along the Silk Road to China?
49673.e: Marco Polo travelled to China over 700 years ago. Later a book was written about his adventures.
49673.m: Marco Polo travelled along the Silk Road to China.

49674.q: What were the inns for traders and their animals on the Silk Road called?
49674.e: A caravanserai was a courtyard surrounded by walls. Traders and animals could stay the night there safely.
49674.m: Traders stayed the night in caravanserais.

49675.q: Apart from silk, which goods were traded on the Silk Road?
49675.e: Spices and precious stones were also traded. Potatoes, maize and tomatoes only came later, from America.
49675.m: Spices were also traded on the Silk Road.

49676.q: Which animal spins the threads that silk is made from?
49676.e: The caterpillar of the silk moth spins itself into a cocoon. Silk is made from this thread.
49676.m: Silk is made from the threads of a caterpillar.

49677.q: How many humps does the Bactrian camel, which often travelled the Silk Road, have?
49677.e: The Bactrian camel is a camel with two humps. It copes well with heat and with great cold too.
49677.m: The Bactrian camel has two humps.

49678.e: Dates contain a lot of sugar. That is why they taste very sweet.

49679.q: Where do date palms grow in the desert?
49679.e: An oasis is a place in the desert with water in the ground. Date palms can grow there.

49680.q: Which plant can be seen above two swords on the coat of arms of Saudi Arabia?
49680.e: Saudi Arabia's coat of arms shows a date palm and two crossed swords. The palm stands for growth and life.
49680.m: There is a palm tree on Saudi Arabia's coat of arms.

49681.e: Date palms come as male trees and female trees. Only the female trees bear dates.
49681.m: Only female date palms bear dates.

49682.q: How tall can a date palm grow?
49682.e: A date palm usually grows 15 to 20 metres tall. That is as tall as a building with about six floors.
49682.m: A date palm can grow about 20 metres tall.

49683.q: What are the large leaves of a palm called?
49683.e: Palms have long, feather-like leaves. These are called fronds.
49683.m: The leaves of a palm are called fronds.

49684.q: During Ramadan, what do many Muslims traditionally break their fast with in the evening?
49684.e: During the fasting month of Ramadan, Muslims eat nothing during the day. In the evening many first eat a date and drink water.
49684.m: During Ramadan the fast is often broken with a date.

49685.q: How do people in Switzerland usually buy dates?
49685.e: Dates do not grow in Switzerland. They are usually imported dried, which makes them keep for a long time.
49685.m: In Switzerland people usually eat dates dried.

49686.q: What does a date palm need to grow?
a: Lots of sun and moist soil
Hardly any light and hardly any water
49686.e: People say the date palm wants its feet in water and its head in the sun. Its roots need water, its crown needs lots of warmth.
49686.m: The date palm needs sun, and water at its roots.

49687.q: What is the big, famous square in the centre of Moscow called?
49687.e: Red Square is right next to the fortress in the centre. The old Russian word for “red” also meant “beautiful”.
49687.m: Red Square is the most famous square in Moscow.

49688.q: What shape are the colourful towers of St Basil's Cathedral in Moscow?
49688.e: St Basil's Cathedral has colourful domes that look like onions. Onion domes like these are typical of Russian churches.
49688.m: Russian churches often have onion-shaped domes.

49689.q: What is a samovar, which used to stand in almost every home in Russia?
49689.e: A samovar is a large metal urn that keeps water hot. In Russia it is traditionally used to make tea.
49689.m: In Russia people make tea with a samovar.

49690.q: Which Russian city used to be the capital and is now the second-largest city?
49690.e: St Petersburg was founded on the Baltic Sea over 300 years ago. For about 200 years it was Russia's capital.
49690.m: St Petersburg used to be Russia's capital.

49691.q: Which animals do many peoples in the north of Siberia keep in large herds?
49691.e: Reindeer can bear great cold. People use their meat and fur and travel around with them.
49691.m: In the north of Siberia many people keep reindeer.

49692.q: What is at the foot of the Burj Khalifa and dances to music in the evening?
49692.e: At the foot of the tower there is a lake with a huge fountain. In the evening its jets of water spray in time to music and lights.
49692.m: There is a dancing fountain at the Burj Khalifa.

49693.q: How do visitors to the Burj Khalifa get up to the viewing platform?
49693.e: Very fast lifts run inside the tower. In about a minute you are high up.
49693.m: Fast lifts take visitors up the Burj Khalifa.

49694.q: What kind of path do people usually take to enter the rock city of Petra?
49694.e: The way into Petra leads through the Siq. This is a narrow gorge with high rock walls.
49694.m: You enter Petra through a narrow gorge.

49695.q: Which gulf is Iran on in the south?
49695.e: To the south Iran borders the Persian Gulf. The gulf is named after Persia, the old name of Iran.
49695.m: In the south Iran is on the Persian Gulf.

49696.q: Which invention from China came west along the Silk Road?
49696.e: The Chinese invented paper. Knowledge of it travelled along the trade routes to Arabia and Europe. Glass and the wheel had long been known in the West, and glasses were invented in Italy.
49696.m: Paper came to us from China along the Silk Road.

49697.q: How many states does the USA have?
49697.e: The USA is made up of 50 states. On top of that, the capital is a separate district.

49698.q: At which mountain in the USA are the faces of four presidents carved into the rock?
49698.e: At Mount Rushmore in South Dakota, four famous presidents are carved into the rock. Each head is about 18 metres tall.
49698.m: At Mount Rushmore you can see four presidents in the rock.

49699.q: In which US city is Hollywood, where many films are made?
49699.e: Hollywood is a district of Los Angeles in California. Many big film studios are there.

49700.q: How many red and white stripes does the flag of the USA have?
49700.e: The 13 stripes recall the first 13 colonies that joined together to form the USA.
49700.m: The 13 stripes on the US flag stand for the first 13 colonies.

49701.q: Which language do most people in the USA speak?
49701.e: In the USA the great majority speak English. Spanish is the second most common language.
49701.m: In the USA people mainly speak English.

49702.q: What is the money in the USA called?
49702.e: In the USA people pay with the US dollar. One dollar has 100 cents.
49702.m: In the USA people pay with dollars.

49703.q: What is the house where the President of the USA lives called?
49703.e: The President of the USA lives and works in the White House in Washington. The Federal Palace is in Bern.
49703.m: The President of the USA lives in the White House.

49704.q: Which ocean lies along the west coast of the USA?
49704.e: To the west the USA borders the Pacific, to the east the Atlantic.
49704.m: The Pacific lies along the west coast of the USA.

49705.q: Which large river flows from north to south through the middle of the USA?
49705.e: The Mississippi is one of the longest rivers in North America. It flows into the Gulf of Mexico.
49705.m: The Mississippi flows through the middle of the USA.

49706.q: What are Canada's two official languages?
49706.e: In Canada both English and French are official languages. Switzerland also has several official languages.
49706.m: Canada has English and French as official languages.

49707.q: By area, where does Canada rank among the largest countries in the world?
49707.e: Only Russia is bigger than Canada. Canada is about 240 times as big as Switzerland.
49707.m: Canada is the second-largest country in the world.

49708.q: Which country lies to the south of Canada?
49708.e: To the south Canada borders the USA. This border is the longest land border in the world between two countries.
49708.m: The USA lies to the south of Canada.

49709.q: Which animal is a national animal of Canada?
49709.e: The beaver has been an official symbol of Canada since 1975. It is even shown on a coin.
49709.m: The beaver is a symbol of Canada.

49710.q: Which sweet syrup is a well-known speciality from Canada?
49710.e: Maple syrup is made by boiling the sap of maple trees. Canada produces most of it.
49710.m: Maple syrup comes mainly from Canada.

49711.q: In which Canadian province do most people speak French?
49711.e: In the province of Quebec, French is the main language. The city of Montreal is there too.
49711.m: In Quebec people mainly speak French.

49712.q: Which is the largest city in Canada?
49712.e: Toronto has the most inhabitants in Canada. The city is on Lake Ontario.
49712.m: Toronto is the largest city in Canada.

49713.q: Which sport is officially Canada's national winter sport?
49713.e: Ice hockey has officially been Canada's national winter sport since 1994. Almost every child there knows the game with puck and stick.
49713.m: Ice hockey is Canada's national winter sport.

49714.q: What are the large areas that Canada is mainly divided into called?
49714.e: Canada has ten provinces and three territories. Switzerland, on the other hand, is divided into cantons.

49715.q: What are the music groups from Mexico with big hats, violins and trumpets called?
49715.e: Mariachi groups play cheerful music from Mexico. The musicians often wear big hats called sombreros.
49715.m: Mariachi is well-known music from Mexico.

49716.q: What is the money in Mexico called?
49716.e: In Mexico people pay with the Mexican peso.
49716.m: In Mexico people pay with pesos.

49717.q: Which country is Mexico's northern neighbour?
49717.e: To the north Mexico borders the USA. To the south are Guatemala and Belize.
49717.m: The USA lies to the north of Mexico.

49718.q: Which ancient people built large pyramids in Mexico?
49718.e: Long ago the Maya built cities with step pyramids, for example Chichén Itzá.
49718.m: The Maya built pyramids in Mexico.

49719.q: Which food originally comes from Mexico?
49719.e: Tacos are filled maize flatbreads from Mexico. Sushi comes from Japan, pizza from Italy and rösti from Switzerland.
49719.m: Tacos are a food from Mexico.

49720.e: Mexico is part of North America, together with the USA and Canada.

49721.q: Which prickly plant grows especially often in the dry areas of Mexico?
49721.e: Cacti store water, so they can live in dry regions. There are very many kinds in Mexico.
49721.m: Lots of cacti grow in Mexico.

49722.q: What colours is the flag of Mexico?
49722.e: Mexico's flag has three stripes in green, white and red. In the middle an eagle sits on a cactus.
49722.m: Mexico's flag is green, white and red.

49723.q: Which old suspension bridge in New York is world-famous?
49723.e: The Brooklyn Bridge connects Manhattan with Brooklyn. The Chapel Bridge is in Lucerne.
49723.m: The Brooklyn Bridge is a famous bridge in New York.

49724.q: Which city has the most inhabitants in the USA?
49724.e: Over 8 million people live in New York. That is more than in any other city in the USA.
49724.m: New York is the largest city in the USA.

49725.q: What is the big park in the middle of New York called?
49725.e: Central Park is a huge park in Manhattan. Hyde Park is in London.
49725.m: Central Park is in the middle of New York.

49726.q: What colour are the well-known taxis in New York?
49726.e: The taxis in New York are yellow. They are called “yellow cabs”.
49726.m: The taxis in New York are yellow.

49727.q: What is the famous square in New York with lots of glowing advertising screens called?
49727.e: In Times Square huge screens glow day and night. Many people celebrate New Year's Eve there.
49727.m: Lots of screens light up Times Square in New York.

49728.q: On which island are most of New York's skyscrapers?
49728.e: Manhattan is a narrow island and a borough of New York. A great many tall buildings stand there.
49728.m: There are lots of skyscrapers in Manhattan.

49729.q: Which large organisation has its headquarters in New York?
49729.e: The United Nations (UN) has its headquarters in New York. The UN also has an important seat in Geneva.
49729.m: The UN headquarters are in New York.

49730.q: What is a very famous old skyscraper in New York called?
49730.e: The Empire State Building was completed in 1931 and was the tallest building in the world for a long time.
49730.m: The Empire State Building is in New York.

49732.q: How do visitors get all the way up into the crown of the Statue of Liberty?
49732.e: There is no lift up to the crown. You have to climb a narrow spiral staircase with lots of steps.
49732.m: You climb a staircase to reach the crown of the Statue of Liberty.

49733.q: What does the Statue of Liberty hold in her raised hand?
49733.e: In her raised right hand she holds a torch. The torch is a sign of the light of freedom.
49733.m: The Statue of Liberty holds a torch up high.

49734.q: What colour is the Statue of Liberty today?
49734.e: Over time, air and rain have turned her metal skin greenish.
49734.m: The Statue of Liberty is greenish today.

49735.q: Which metal is the outer skin of the Statue of Liberty made of?
49735.e: The skin is made of thin copper sheets. In the air, copper forms a green layer called patina.
49735.m: The skin of the Statue of Liberty is made of copper.

49736.q: What does the Statue of Liberty wear on her head?
49736.e: Her crown has seven points like rays of the sun.
49736.m: The Statue of Liberty wears a crown with rays.

49737.q: Where exactly does the Statue of Liberty stand?
a: In the middle of a park
On top of a tower block
49737.e: She stands on Liberty Island, a small island in the harbour. You reach it by boat.
49737.m: The Statue of Liberty stands on an island.

49738.q: Which famous engineer built the iron framework inside the Statue of Liberty?
49738.e: Gustave Eiffel built the supporting framework inside. Later he built the Eiffel Tower in Paris.
49738.m: Gustave Eiffel built the framework of the Statue of Liberty.

49739.q: Which date is written on the tablet the Statue of Liberty holds in her arm?
49739.e: On 4 July 1776 the USA declared its independence. That is why 4 July is the national holiday there.
49739.m: The tablet of the Statue of Liberty shows the USA's Independence Day.

49740.q: Which river carved out the Grand Canyon?
49740.e: The Colorado River slowly ate its way deep into the rock. That is how the huge gorge was formed.
49740.m: The Colorado River shaped the Grand Canyon.

49741.q: In which country is the Grand Canyon?
49741.e: The Grand Canyon is in the south-west of the USA.
49741.m: The Grand Canyon is in the USA.

49742.e: A canyon is a deep gorge with steep walls. “Grand” means large.
49742.m: The Grand Canyon is a huge gorge.

49743.q: In which US state is the Grand Canyon?
49743.e: The Grand Canyon is in the state of Arizona in the south-west of the USA.
49743.m: The Grand Canyon is in Arizona.

49744.q: About how deep is the Grand Canyon at its deepest points?
49744.e: At its deepest points the gorge is about 1,800 metres deep. That is roughly the height of the Rigi above sea level.
49744.m: The Grand Canyon is almost 2 kilometres deep.

49745.q: What colours are the rock walls of the Grand Canyon mainly?
49745.e: The layers of rock glow mainly red, orange and brown, especially in the evening.
49745.m: The rocks in the Grand Canyon are red and orange.

49746.q: How long did it take for the Grand Canyon to form?
49746.e: Over millions of years the river wore away the rock bit by bit.
49746.m: The Grand Canyon formed over millions of years.

49747.q: What has the Grand Canyon been since 1919?
49747.e: The Grand Canyon has been a national park since 1919. That way the nature there is protected.
49747.m: The Grand Canyon is a protected national park.

49748.q: Which park is considered the first national park in the world?
49748.e: Yellowstone was the first national park in the world. The Swiss National Park in the Engadine was founded in 1914.
49748.m: Yellowstone is the oldest national park in the world.

49749.q: What shoots up into the air from a geyser?
49749.e: A geyser is a hot spring that keeps shooting hot water and steam into the air. There are hundreds of them in Yellowstone.
49749.m: A geyser shoots hot water into the air.

49750.q: Where do the bright colours of some hot springs in Yellowstone National Park come from?
a: From tiny living things in the water
From paint that people pour in
From red-hot lava in the water
49750.e: Tiny living things live in the hot water. They colour the springs blue, green, yellow and orange.
49750.m: Tiny living things make the hot springs in Yellowstone colourful.

49751.q: Which large animal with thick fur lives in herds in Yellowstone?
49751.e: Thousands of bison live in Yellowstone. This herd has lived wild there for a very long time.
49751.m: Bison live in herds in Yellowstone.

49752.q: Which predator was brought back to Yellowstone in 1995?
49752.e: Wolves had once been wiped out there. In 1995 wolves were brought back to the park. The wolf has also returned to Switzerland.
49752.m: Since 1995 wolves have lived in Yellowstone again.

49753.q: Which kind of bear lives in Yellowstone National Park?
49753.e: Grizzly bears and black bears live in Yellowstone. Polar bears live in the far north, pandas in China.

49754.q: What lies deep beneath Yellowstone National Park?
49754.e: Beneath the park lies a huge volcano with hot rock. That is why the water in many springs there is so hot.
49754.m: A huge volcano lies beneath Yellowstone.

49755.q: In which mountain range in North America is Yellowstone National Park?
49755.e: Yellowstone is in the Rocky Mountains in the west of the USA. Most of the park is in the state of Wyoming.
49755.m: Yellowstone is in the Rocky Mountains.

49756.q: Which US state is the largest?
49756.e: Alaska is by far the largest state, more than twice as big as Texas.
49756.m: Alaska is the largest state in the USA.

49757.q: From which country did the USA buy Alaska in 1867?
49757.e: In 1867 the USA bought Alaska from Russia for 7.2 million dollars.
49757.m: The USA bought Alaska from Russia.

49758.q: What is the highest mountain in North America, which is in Alaska, called?
49758.e: Denali is over 6,100 metres high. It is much higher than the Dufourspitze, the highest peak in Switzerland.
49758.m: Denali in Alaska is the highest mountain in North America.

49759.q: Which country does Alaska share a land border with?
49759.e: To the east Alaska borders Canada. Between Alaska and Russia there is only a strait.

49760.q: Which large animals often catch salmon in Alaska's rivers?
49760.e: In summer the salmon swim up the rivers. Then the brown bears catch them with their paws and mouths.
49760.m: In Alaska brown bears catch salmon.

49761.q: Which coloured lights do you often see in the night sky in Alaska?
49761.e: The northern lights glow green or pink in the sky. You see them mainly in areas close to the North Pole.
49761.m: You often see the northern lights in Alaska.

49762.q: What is the capital of Alaska?
49762.e: The capital is Juneau. But the largest city is Anchorage.
49762.m: The capital of Alaska is Juneau.

49763.q: Which famous race takes place in Alaska every year?
49763.e: In the Iditarod, people drive dog sleds well over 1,000 kilometres through snow and ice.
49763.m: Alaska has a famous sled dog race.

49764.q: Which country is Ottawa the capital of?
49764.e: Ottawa is the capital of Canada. The country's Parliament meets there.
49764.m: Ottawa is the capital of Canada.

49765.q: In which Canadian province is Ottawa?
49765.e: Ottawa is in the province of Ontario, right on the border with Quebec.
49765.m: Ottawa is in the province of Ontario.

49766.e: The city is on the Ottawa River. There the river forms the border between two provinces.
49766.m: Ottawa is on the Ottawa River.

49767.q: What do lots of people do on the Rideau Canal in Ottawa in winter?
49767.e: In winter the canal freezes over. Then it becomes a very long ice rink in the middle of the city.
49767.m: In winter people skate on the canal in Ottawa.

49768.q: Which flowers do the Netherlands send to Ottawa every year as a thank-you?
49768.e: Canada helped to free the Netherlands in the Second World War. As thanks, tulip bulbs arrive every year, and Ottawa holds a tulip festival.
49768.m: Every year tulips from the Netherlands bloom in Ottawa.

49769.q: Which British queen chose Ottawa as the capital of Canada?
49769.e: The British Queen Victoria chose Ottawa as the capital in 1857.
49769.m: Queen Victoria chose Ottawa as the capital.

49770.q: Where does the city of Ottawa get its name from?
49770.e: The name comes from the Odawa people, who used to trade in the area.
49770.m: Ottawa is named after an Indigenous people.

49771.q: What is the capital of Mexico?
49771.e: The capital is called Mexico City, in Spanish “Ciudad de México”.
49771.m: The capital of Mexico is Mexico City.

49772.q: Which Aztec city used to stand where Mexico City is today?
49772.e: Tenochtitlan was the capital of the Aztecs. The Spanish destroyed it and built a new city on top of it.
49772.m: Mexico City stands on the old Aztec city of Tenochtitlan.

49773.q: Where did the Aztecs build their city in the Valley of Mexico?
a: On an island in a lake
49773.e: The Aztecs founded their city on an island in a large lake. Later the lake was almost completely drained.
49773.m: The Aztecs built their capital on an island in a lake.

49774.q: About how high above sea level is Mexico City?
49774.e: Mexico City is about 2,240 metres above sea level. That is higher than the Gotthard Pass.
49774.m: Mexico City lies very high up.

49775.q: What is the big main square of Mexico City called?
49775.e: The Zócalo is one of the largest squares in the world. The cathedral and the National Palace stand there.
49775.m: The big square in Mexico City is called the Zócalo.

49776.q: In which city is the famous Estadio Azteca football stadium?
49776.e: The finals of the 1970 and 1986 Football World Cups took place in the Estadio Azteca in Mexico City.
49776.m: The Estadio Azteca is in Mexico City.

49777.q: About how many people live in the Greater Mexico City area?
49777.e: Over 20 million people live in the Greater Mexico City area. That is more than twice as many as in the whole of Switzerland.
49777.m: Mexico City is one of the largest cities in the world.

49778.q: Which natural hazard happens again and again in Mexico City?
49778.e: Mexico City lies in an area where the earth often moves. That is why there are earthquakes there again and again.
49778.m: There are often earthquakes in Mexico City.

49779.q: There is a district with old canals in Mexico City. What do people travel in there?
49779.e: In the Xochimilco district, colourful boats travel along old canals. The canals are what is left of a large lake.
49779.m: In Xochimilco people travel along canals in colourful boats.

49780.q: In which city is the Golden Gate Bridge?
49780.e: The Golden Gate Bridge connects San Francisco with the land to the north.
49780.m: The Golden Gate Bridge is in San Francisco.

49781.q: What colour is the Golden Gate Bridge?
49781.e: The bridge is not golden but orange-red. That way it can be seen well even in fog.
49781.m: The Golden Gate Bridge is orange-red.

49782.q: What kind of bridge is the Golden Gate Bridge?
49782.e: The roadway hangs from thick steel cables that run over two tall towers.
49782.m: The Golden Gate Bridge is a suspension bridge.

49783.q: In which year was the Golden Gate Bridge opened?
49783.e: The bridge opened in 1937. At that time it was the longest suspension bridge in the world.
49783.m: The Golden Gate Bridge has been open since 1937.

49784.q: What does the Golden Gate Bridge cross?
49784.e: The “Golden Gate” is a strait between the Pacific and San Francisco Bay.
49784.m: The Golden Gate Bridge crosses a strait.

49785.q: What often hides the Golden Gate Bridge almost completely?
49785.e: Thick fog often rolls into the bay from the sea. Then you can only see the tops of the towers.
49785.m: The Golden Gate Bridge is often in fog.

49786.q: Which former prison island lies in the bay near the Golden Gate Bridge?
49786.e: Alcatraz was a well-known prison on an island in San Francisco Bay. Today the island is a museum that you can visit (as of 2025).
49786.m: Alcatraz is a prison island near San Francisco.

49787.q: In which US state is the Golden Gate Bridge?
49787.e: San Francisco and the bridge are in California on the west coast.
49787.m: The Golden Gate Bridge is in California.

49788.q: Which leaf is on the flag of Canada?
49788.e: In the middle of the Canadian flag there is a maple leaf. Maple trees are very common in Canada.
49788.m: There is a maple leaf on Canada's flag.

49789.q: What colour is the maple leaf on the flag of Canada?
49789.e: The maple leaf is red, like the autumn leaves of many maple trees.
49789.m: The maple leaf on Canada's flag is red.

49790.q: How many points does the maple leaf on Canada's flag have?
49790.e: The leaf on the flag is drawn in a simple way and has exactly eleven points.
49790.m: The maple leaf on the flag has eleven points.

49791.q: Which leaf is shown on the flag of Canada?
49791.e: The red and white flag with the red maple leaf was introduced in 1965. The maple is the symbol of Canada.
49791.m: There is a maple leaf on Canada's flag.

49792.q: What colour is the square in the middle of Canada's flag?
49792.e: The flag has a red stripe on the left and on the right. In between there is a white square.
49792.m: There is a white area in the middle of Canada's flag.

49793.q: What do many Canadians call their flag?
49793.e: The flag is named after the maple leaf on it. Old Glory is a name for the US flag, and the Union Jack is the British flag.
49793.m: Canada's flag is also called “The Maple Leaf”.

49794.q: What happens to the leaves of many maple trees in Canada in autumn?
49794.e: In autumn the maple forests in Canada turn bright colours. That attracts lots of tourists.
49794.m: Maple leaves glow red and orange in autumn.

49795.q: What colours is the flag of Canada?
49795.e: Canada's flag has two red stripes and, in the middle, a white area with a red maple leaf.
49795.m: Canada's flag is red and white.

49796.q: What is the capital of Costa Rica?
49796.e: The capital of Costa Rica is San José. It lies in a valley in the middle of the country.
49796.m: The capital of Costa Rica is San José.

49797.q: What has Costa Rica not had since 1948?
49797.e: Costa Rica abolished its army in 1948. Since then the money has been spent mainly on schools and health.
49797.m: Costa Rica is a country without an army.

49798.q: Which language is spoken in Costa Rica?
49798.e: Spanish is the official language in Costa Rica. That goes back to the time when Spain ruled the country.
49798.m: In Costa Rica people speak Spanish.

49799.q: What does the name “Costa Rica” mean in English?
49799.e: “Costa” means coast and “rica” means rich. The Spanish gave the country this name.

49800.q: Which slow animal often hangs upside down in the trees in Costa Rica?
49800.e: Sloths live in the rainforests of Costa Rica. They move very slowly and usually hang upside down from branches.
49800.m: The sloth hangs slowly and comfortably in the trees.

49801.q: What does Costa Rica have lots of, for example Arenal?
49801.e: Costa Rica has many volcanoes, and some are still active. Arenal in the north is one of the best known.

49802.q: Which saying is very popular in Costa Rica and means something like “pure life”?
49802.e: People in Costa Rica often say “Pura vida”. They use it to say hello, to say thank you and when they are feeling good.
49802.m: In Costa Rica people like to say “Pura vida”.

49803.q: Which country borders Costa Rica to the north?
49803.e: Nicaragua lies to the north of Costa Rica. Cuba is an island and Colombia lies further south.
49803.m: Nicaragua is Costa Rica's northern neighbour.

49804.q: Which two seas does Costa Rica border?
49804.e: Costa Rica has a coast on the Pacific to the west and one on the Caribbean Sea to the east.
49804.m: Costa Rica lies between the Pacific and the Caribbean Sea.
