49805.q: What kind of cars do you see especially often in the streets of Havana?
49805.e: In Cuba many old cars from the 1950s are still on the road. They are repaired again and again.
49805.m: Lots of colourful vintage cars drive around Havana.

49806.q: Which US state lies close to the north of Cuba?
49806.e: Only about 150 kilometres of sea lie between Cuba and Florida. The southern tip of Florida is the southernmost point of the US mainland.
49806.m: Florida is not far north of Cuba.

49807.q: Which plant is grown a lot in Cuba to make sugar?
49807.e: Lots of sugar cane grows in Cuba. Sugar is made from the sweet juice of the stalks.
49807.m: In Cuba sugar is made from sugar cane.

49808.q: How many stars does the flag of Cuba have?
49808.e: Cuba's flag has a white star in a red triangle. There are also blue and white stripes.
49808.m: A single star shines on Cuba's flag.

49809.q: What is the money in Cuba called?
49809.e: In Cuba people pay with the Cuban peso. Peso is a Spanish word.
49809.m: In Cuba people pay with the peso.

49810.q: Why is the Cuban crocodile especially worth protecting?
a: It only lives wild in Cuba and is rare
It is the largest animal on Earth
It only lives in the open sea
It is the only crocodile in America
49810.e: The Cuban crocodile only lives wild in a few swamps in Cuba. It is rare and strictly protected.
49810.m: The Cuban crocodile only lives in Cuba.

49811.q: What is the capital of Jamaica?
49811.e: Kingston is the capital of Jamaica. It has a large harbour.
49811.m: The capital of Jamaica is Kingston.

49812.q: What is the official language in Jamaica?
49812.e: Jamaica belonged to Great Britain for a long time. That is why English is the official language.
49812.m: English is the official language in Jamaica.

49813.e: Reggae began in Jamaica in the 1960s. Today it is heard all over the world.
49813.m: Reggae is the well-known music from Jamaica.

49814.q: Which famous reggae singer came from Jamaica?
49814.e: Bob Marley was born in Jamaica. With his songs he made reggae famous around the world.
49814.m: Bob Marley is the best-known reggae singer from Jamaica.

49815.q: Which very fast runner comes from Jamaica?
49815.e: Usain Bolt is a sprinter from Jamaica. In 2009 he ran the 100 metres in a world record time of 9.58 seconds.
49815.m: Usain Bolt from Jamaica is one of the fastest runners in the world.

49816.q: What are the well-known mountains in Jamaica where coffee grows called?
49816.e: The Blue Mountains are the highest mountains in Jamaica. A famous coffee grows there.
49816.m: Coffee grows in the Blue Mountains in Jamaica.

49817.q: What colours is the flag of Jamaica?
49817.e: Jamaica's flag has a yellow cross in the shape of an X. The areas in between are green and black.
49817.m: Jamaica's flag is green, yellow and black.

49818.q: With which winter sport did Jamaica become famous at the 1988 Olympic Games?
49818.e: In 1988 a bobsleigh team from Jamaica took part in the Winter Olympics for the first time. Many people were amazed, because there is no snow in Jamaica.
49818.m: A bobsleigh team from Jamaica took part in the 1988 Winter Olympics.

49819.q: What is the capital of Guatemala?
49819.e: The capital has almost the same name as the country. It is called Guatemala City.
49819.m: The capital of Guatemala is Guatemala City.

49820.q: What is the colourful national bird of Guatemala called?
49820.e: The quetzal has green and red feathers and a very long tail. It is even on Guatemala's flag.
49820.m: The quetzal is the national bird of Guatemala.

49821.q: Which ancient Maya city lies in the rainforest of Guatemala?
49821.e: Tikal was a large city of the Maya. Its tall temples now stand in the middle of the rainforest.
49821.m: Tikal is an ancient Maya city in Guatemala.

49822.q: What stands around Lake Atitlán in the highlands of Guatemala?
49822.e: Lake Atitlán lies in the highlands of Guatemala. Three volcanoes stand around it.
49822.m: Lake Atitlán in Guatemala is surrounded by volcanoes.

49823.q: Which country borders Guatemala to the north?
49823.e: Guatemala has a long border with Mexico to the north and west.

49824.q: Which ancient people lived in Guatemala and still have many descendants there today?
49824.e: Many descendants of the Maya live in Guatemala. Many still speak a Maya language today.
49824.m: Many Maya still live in Guatemala today.

49825.q: What are many Maya women in Guatemala known for?
49825.e: Many Maya women wear colourful hand-woven blouses and skirts. Each village often has its own patterns.
49825.m: In Guatemala the Maya weave colourful fabrics.

49826.q: What colours is the flag of Guatemala?
49826.e: Guatemala's flag has two light blue stripes and a white stripe in the middle.
49826.m: Guatemala's flag is light blue and white.

49827.q: In which country is the Maya pyramid of Chichén Itzá?
49827.e: Chichén Itzá is in the south of Mexico. Every year a great many people visit the old buildings.

49828.q: What did the Maya build the great pyramid at Chichén Itzá for?
a: As a temple for a god
As a tomb for a pharaoh
49828.e: On top of the pyramid there is a temple. It was dedicated to the god Kukulcán, a feathered serpent. Tombs for pharaohs were built in Egypt.
49828.m: The pyramid at Chichén Itzá was a temple.

49829.q: Which people built the city of Chichén Itzá?
49829.e: Chichén Itzá was a large city of the Maya. It was built over 1,000 years ago.

49830.q: What is Chichén Itzá in Mexico known for?
a: For a large Maya step pyramid
49830.e: The great pyramid El Castillo stands at Chichén Itzá. The Maya built it over 1,000 years ago.
49830.m: A large Maya pyramid stands at Chichén Itzá.

49831.q: How many sides of the El Castillo pyramid have a staircase?
49831.e: The pyramid has a staircase on all four sides. They lead up to a temple.
49831.m: The El Castillo pyramid has a staircase on four sides.

49832.q: How many steps does the El Castillo pyramid have if you count the top platform too?
49832.e: Each of the four staircases has 91 steps. 4 times 91 makes 364, and with the platform it is 365, as many as there are days in the year.
49832.m: The pyramid has as many steps as the year has days.

49833.q: Which animal seems to crawl down the pyramid's staircase as a shadow in spring?
49833.e: In spring and autumn the sun casts shadows on the staircase. It looks as if a snake is crawling down.
49833.m: At Chichén Itzá a shadow snake crawls down the staircase in spring.

49834.q: Which famous list has Chichén Itzá been on since 2007?
a: New Seven Wonders of the World
49834.e: In 2007 Chichén Itzá was chosen as one of the “New Seven Wonders of the World”.
49834.m: Chichén Itzá is one of the New Seven Wonders of the World.

49835.q: The Caribbean is a warm sea with many islands. Where is it?
a: Between North America and South America
49835.e: The Caribbean Sea lies between Central America, South America and many islands. It is warm there all year round.
49835.m: The Caribbean lies between North and South America.

49836.q: Why are the Caribbean islands also called the “West Indies”?
a: Columbus thought he was in India
49836.e: Christopher Columbus wanted to sail to India. When he reached America, he thought he was in India.
49836.m: The Caribbean is called the West Indies because Columbus made a mistake.

49837.q: Which country does the Caribbean island of Puerto Rico belong to?
49837.e: Puerto Rico is an overseas territory of the USA. The people there speak Spanish and English.
49837.m: Puerto Rico belongs to the USA.

49838.q: On which Caribbean island do people speak French because it belongs to France?
49838.e: Martinique belongs to France. People there even pay with the euro.
49838.m: On Martinique in the Caribbean people speak French.

49839.q: Which people is the Caribbean named after?
49839.e: The Caribs were Indigenous people who lived on many islands and along the coasts. The Caribbean got its name from them.
49839.m: The Caribbean is named after the Carib people.

49840.q: Who used to make the Caribbean unsafe with their ships and attack other ships?
49840.e: About 300 years ago there were many pirates in the Caribbean. They attacked ships carrying gold and goods.
49840.m: In the past pirates attacked many ships in the Caribbean.

49841.q: Which musical instrument made from old oil drums comes from Trinidad and Tobago?
49841.e: The steel pan is made from an oil drum. It comes from Trinidad and Tobago and sounds bright and cheerful.
49841.m: The steel pan from Trinidad is made from an oil drum.

49842.q: What grows underwater in the warm Caribbean Sea and is very colourful?
49842.e: Coral reefs grow in the warm, clear water of the Caribbean. Lots of colourful fish live there.
49842.m: There are colourful coral reefs in the Caribbean.

49843.e: A hurricane is a very powerful spinning storm. It brings fierce winds and lots of rain.
49843.m: A hurricane is a very powerful tropical storm.

49844.e: A hurricane needs warm seawater. That is where it gets its power from.

49845.q: What is the calm centre of a hurricane called?
49845.e: In the middle of a hurricane there is hardly any wind and it is often even clear. This spot is called the eye.
49845.m: The eye is the calm centre of a hurricane.

49846.q: What does every hurricane get so that it can be easily recognised?
49846.e: Every hurricane gets a first name, for example from a fixed list. That makes it easier to tell them apart.
49846.m: Every hurricane gets its own name.

49847.q: What is such a tropical storm called when it forms in the Pacific near Asia?
49847.e: In the western Pacific near Asia these storms are called typhoons. Over the Atlantic they are called hurricanes.
49847.m: Near Asia a hurricane is called a typhoon.

49848.q: How many levels of strength does the scale for hurricanes have?
49848.e: Hurricanes are divided into categories 1 to 5. Category 5 is the strongest.
49848.m: Hurricanes have five levels of strength.

49849.q: What do scientists use to watch a hurricane from high above?
49849.e: Satellites in space take pictures of hurricanes. That shows where the storm is heading.

49850.q: Which group of birds does the smallest bird in the world belong to?
49850.e: The smallest bird in the world is a hummingbird from Cuba. It is only about 5 to 6 centimetres long and weighs about 2 grams.
49850.m: The smallest bird in the world is a hummingbird.

49851.q: What do hummingbirds like to drink most?
49851.e: Hummingbirds sip sweet nectar from flowers. They also eat small insects.

49852.q: What can a hummingbird do that almost no other bird can?
49852.e: Hummingbirds can fly forwards, sideways and even backwards. Many birds can stand on one leg, glide and build nests.
49852.m: A hummingbird can even fly backwards.

49853.q: What is it called when a hummingbird stays in one spot in the air?
49853.e: When hovering, the hummingbird moves its wings very fast. That way it stays still in the air in front of a flower.
49853.m: When hovering, the hummingbird stands still in the air.

49854.q: How often does a small hummingbird beat its wings?
a: Many dozens of times per second
49854.e: Small hummingbirds beat their wings many dozens of times per second. That is why you can hardly see the wings.
49854.m: A hummingbird's wings beat as fast as lightning.

49855.q: On which continent do hummingbirds live in the wild?
49855.e: Hummingbirds only live wild in North, Central and South America. Most species are in South America.
49855.m: Hummingbirds only live wild in America.

49856.q: Why is the hummingbird called a “hummingbird”?
49856.e: To hum means to make a low buzzing sound. The hummingbird's fast wings make a humming noise.

49857.q: How does the hummingbird reach the nectar deep inside the flower?
49857.e: The hummingbird has a long, thin beak and a long tongue. With them it reaches the nectar deep inside the flower.
49857.m: The hummingbird has a long beak for nectar.

49858.q: What is the capital of the Dominican Republic?
49858.e: Santo Domingo is the capital of the Dominican Republic. It is on the south coast.
49858.m: The capital of the Dominican Republic is Santo Domingo.

49859.q: Which country does the Dominican Republic share an island with?
49859.e: The island of Hispaniola is divided into two countries. Haiti is in the west, the Dominican Republic in the east.
49859.m: The Dominican Republic shares its island with Haiti.

49860.q: In which sea is the island the Dominican Republic is on?
49860.e: The Dominican Republic is on the island of Hispaniola in the Caribbean. Pico Duarte, the highest mountain in the Caribbean, is there too.
49860.m: The Dominican Republic is in the Caribbean.

49861.q: Which sport is especially popular in the Dominican Republic?
49861.e: Baseball is very popular in the Dominican Republic. Many players from there play in the USA.
49861.m: People in the Dominican Republic love playing baseball.

49862.q: Which dance comes from the Dominican Republic?
49862.e: The merengue is a fast, cheerful dance. It is the national dance of the Dominican Republic.
49862.m: The merengue comes from the Dominican Republic.

49863.q: Which book can be seen in the coat of arms on the flag of the Dominican Republic?
49863.e: In the middle of the flag there is a coat of arms with an open Bible. No other national flag has this.
49863.m: A Bible is shown on the flag of the Dominican Republic.

49864.q: What is special about the city of Santo Domingo in the Dominican Republic?
49864.e: Santo Domingo was founded by the Spanish over 500 years ago. It is the oldest city still lived in that Europeans founded in America.
49864.m: Santo Domingo is the oldest European city in America.

49865.q: What is chocolate made from, which is grown a lot in the Dominican Republic?
49865.e: Many cocoa trees grow in the Dominican Republic. Chocolate is made from the cocoa beans.

49866.q: What is the capital of the Bahamas?
49866.e: Nassau is the capital of the Bahamas. It is on the island of New Providence.
49866.m: The capital of the Bahamas is Nassau.

49867.q: What is the official language in the Bahamas?
49867.e: The Bahamas belonged to Great Britain for a long time. That is why people speak English there.
49867.m: In the Bahamas people speak English.

49868.q: About how many islands make up the Bahamas?
49868.e: The Bahamas are made up of about 700 islands. On top of that there are many tiny rocks and sandbanks. People live on only a few of the islands.
49868.m: The Bahamas are made up of about 700 islands.

49869.q: Which animals swim in the sea on an island in the Bahamas and are famous for it?
49869.e: On a small island in the Bahamas pigs live on the beach. They swim out to the visitors' boats.
49869.m: There are swimming pigs in the Bahamas.

49870.q: Where did Christopher Columbus first set foot on land in America in 1492?
49870.e: Columbus landed on an island in the Bahamas in October 1492. The Indigenous people called it Guanahani.
49870.m: In 1492 Columbus landed first in the Bahamas.

49871.q: Which pink bird is the national bird of the Bahamas?
49871.e: The flamingo is the national bird of the Bahamas. Very many of them live on the island of Inagua.
49871.m: The flamingo is the national bird of the Bahamas.

49872.q: In which ocean are the Bahamas?
49872.e: The Bahamas are in the Atlantic Ocean, south-east of Florida. They are not in the Caribbean Sea.
49872.m: The Bahamas are in the Atlantic.

49873.q: From which country did the Bahamas become independent in 1973?
49873.e: The Bahamas were a British colony. In 1973 they became a state of their own.
49873.m: The Bahamas have been independent since 1973.

49874.q: What is the fruit of the coconut palm called?
49874.e: Coconuts grow on the coconut palm. They hang at the top under the leaves.
49874.m: The fruit of the coconut palm is called a coconut.

49875.q: What is inside a young, green coconut?
49875.e: Young coconuts contain lots of clear coconut water. You can drink it straight from the nut.

49876.q: Is the coconut a true nut for plant scientists?
49876.e: The coconut is actually a stone fruit, like the cherry or the plum. Even so, it is called a nut.
49876.m: The coconut is actually a stone fruit.

49877.q: How do coconuts get to other islands by themselves?
49877.e: Coconuts are light and waterproof. They can drift in the sea for a long time and sprout on another beach.
49877.m: Coconuts can float across the sea.

49878.q: How many small dark spots, the “eyes”, does a coconut have?
49878.e: A coconut has three dark spots. The new palm grows out of one of them.

49879.q: How tall can a coconut palm grow?
49879.e: A coconut palm can grow up to about 30 metres tall. That is as tall as a building with ten floors.
49879.m: A coconut palm can grow up to 30 metres tall.

49880.q: What is made from the white flesh of the coconut?
49880.e: The white flesh is grated and squeezed. That makes coconut milk for cooking. Coconut water is already inside the young nut.
49880.m: Coconut milk is made from the flesh of the coconut.

49881.q: What is made from the fibres of the coconut shell?
49881.e: On the outside, the coconut has a layer of tough fibres. These are used to make ropes, brushes and doormats.
49881.m: Doormats are made from coconut fibres.

49882.q: Where do coconut palms especially like to grow?
49882.e: Coconut palms need warmth and lots of sun. They often grow on sandy beaches in the tropics.
49882.m: Coconut palms grow on warm beaches in the tropics.

49883.q: Which country does the famous “Panama hat” actually come from?
49883.e: The Panama hat is woven in Ecuador. It got its name because it was sold via Panama.
49883.m: The Panama hat actually comes from Ecuador.

49884.q: How many stars does the flag of Panama have?
49884.e: Panama's flag has four sections. In each of the two white sections there is a star, one blue and one red.
49884.m: There are two stars on Panama's flag.

49885.q: Which large bird of prey of the rainforest is the national bird of Panama?
49885.e: The harpy eagle is a very powerful bird of prey of the rainforest. It is the national bird of Panama.
49885.m: The harpy eagle is the national bird of Panama.

49886.q: Which golden-yellow animal is a symbol of good luck in Panama?
49886.e: The Panamanian golden frog is seen as a lucky charm in Panama. Today it is very rare and seriously endangered.
49886.m: The golden frog is a symbol of good luck in Panama.

49887.q: Panama is a narrow country. Which two continents does it connect?
49887.e: Panama lies between North America and South America. It is like a narrow bridge of land.
49887.m: Panama connects North America and South America.

49888.q: Which money do people in Panama mostly use in everyday life?
49888.e: Panama does have its own money, the balboa. But in everyday life people mostly pay with US dollars.
49888.m: In Panama people mostly pay with US dollars.

49889.q: Cuba's national bird has the colours of the Cuban flag. Which colours are they?
49889.e: The tocororo has red, white and blue feathers. These are the colours of the Cuban flag.
49889.m: Cuba's national bird is red, white and blue.

49890.q: What can a hurricane often cause on the coast?
49890.e: A hurricane brings heavy rain and pushes the sea onto the coast. Then the land is often flooded.

49891.q: On which Caribbean island is Dutch an official language?
49891.e: Curaçao is part of the Kingdom of the Netherlands. That is why Dutch is an official language there.
49891.m: Dutch is an official language on Curaçao.

49892.q: What does a hummingbird do at night to save energy?
a: It goes into a kind of deep sleep called torpor
49892.e: At night the hummingbird becomes completely still and cools down. In this torpor it needs much less energy.
49892.m: Hummingbirds save energy at night in torpor.

49893.q: Where did the Maya in Chichén Itzá get their drinking water from?
a: From deep water holes in the ground
49893.e: There are hardly any rivers on the Yucatán Peninsula. The Maya got water from cenotes, which are deep water holes in the limestone.
49893.m: The Maya got water from deep water holes.

49894.q: Which is the largest city in Brazil?
49894.e: In the 2022 census, over 11 million people lived in São Paulo. It is the largest city in all of South America.
49894.m: São Paulo is the largest city in Brazil.

49895.q: About how many people live in Brazil (as of 2022)?
49895.e: The 2022 census counted about 203 million people. That is more than twenty times as many as in Switzerland.
49895.m: About 200 million people live in Brazil.

49896.q: Which famous footballer from Brazil won the World Cup three times?
49896.e: Pelé won the World Cup in 1958, 1962 and 1970. No other player has done that.
49896.m: Pelé won the World Cup three times.

49897.q: How many times has Brazil won the men's football World Cup (as of 2026)?
49897.e: Brazil won the World Cup in 1958, 1962, 1970, 1994 and 2002. No country has won more often.
49897.m: Brazil has won the football World Cup five times.

49898.q: What colour is the background of Brazil's flag?
49898.e: Brazil's flag is green with a yellow diamond. In the middle there is a blue globe with stars.
49898.m: Brazil's flag is green with a yellow diamond.

49899.q: What is the name of the martial art from Brazil that looks like a dance with music?
49899.e: Capoeira began in Brazil. You move to music and singing, almost like dancing.
49899.m: Capoeira is a martial art from Brazil.

49900.q: Which big festival with parades and samba is famous in Brazil?
49900.e: Carnival takes place every year before Lent. Thousands of people then dance through the streets in colourful costumes.

49901.q: Which dance began in Argentina and Uruguay?
49901.e: The tango began over 100 years ago in the port cities on the Río de la Plata. It is danced by two people in a close embrace.
49901.m: The tango comes from Argentina and Uruguay.

49902.q: Which country won the men's football World Cup in 2022?
49902.e: In 2022 in Qatar, Argentina beat France in the final on penalties. It was Argentina's third title.
49902.m: Argentina won the football World Cup in 2022.

49903.q: What is the name of Argentina's southernmost city, often called the “End of the World”?
49903.e: Ushuaia lies right in the south on the coast. Many ships to Antarctica set off from there.
49903.m: Ushuaia is seen as the southernmost city in the world.

49904.q: What is the name of the popular barbecue with lots of meat in Argentina?
49904.e: At an asado, meat is grilled slowly over hot embers. Families and friends often meet for it at the weekend.
49904.m: The asado is a barbecue in Argentina.
